beat_player.text: {player} pressed hard today. Rest your {troop_count} men before the next march, the road is long and the ford is cold.
Ser {player}, that flank was clever and it cost me {troop_count} men. Join me at the inn tonight. The ale is on me.
You won this field, {player}, and I will not pretend otherwise. I have seen harder men lose harder fields. Keep your {gold} gold, ser, and watch the ford ahead.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat me fair today and cost me {troop_count} men. Good play deserves praise. I will remember this field.
Ser {player}, your center held and I lost {troop_count} men to my own impatience. I will learn from that.
{player}, you have won this round and I will not dispute the ledger. I have written down worse losses than {troop_count} men, and I survived every one. Ride on, and mind the marsh road.

fought_alongside_player.text: {player} and I broke the {enemy_faction} line with {troop_count} men behind us. Shoulder to shoulder, as it was in the first war.
Ser {player}, your flank held firm against {enemy_faction}. Stay close on the next march, and I will show you a crossing.
Good work out there, {player}. Those {troop_count} soldiers did their part and so did you. The {enemy_faction} will remember this field, and so will I.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me go without ransom. I keep a ledger of debts, and I will remember this kindness.
{player} released me without ransom today. Mercy is rarer on these roads than gold, and I will not forget who gave it freely.
Ser {player}, you freed me rather than take my coin. I do not trust it yet, but I have written it down. Mercy has its own weight.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome to the banner. Ask me anything about the roads, I have walked them since the first war.
Ser {player}, you chose {my_faction} and I will not forget it. Find me when the banners are quiet and I will show you the crossing.
Ser {player}, a new oath under {my_faction}. Oaths are cheap at the gate and dear on the road. I hope you can carry yours.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} has gone to {player}. I have watched this land change hands many times. Keep the granary full and the gates honest.
Ser {player}, {fief} is a heavy gift. Walls do not hold themselves, and I have seen many granaries empty in hard winters.
Ser {player}, {fief} went to you while others waited years. I am not bitter, only curious. Keep your record clean, I keep mine.

encounter_greeting.text: Well met on the road, {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have walked this way since the first war. Ride with care.
Ah, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} at your service, though service is a generous word for an old traveler. Does your party need anything before the ford?
{player}, I see your banner and I see your party's size. {persona} of {my_faction} keeps no quarrel on this road unless you give me cause. Keep your distance and we will part well.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. Keep your men fed and your eyes on the ford, and find me at the inn when we next cross paths.
We part here, {player}. Mind the marsh road past the bend, it has swallowed better riders than you. Until the next crossing.
Go on, {player}. Our words are finished for today, and I would rather not hear more of your banner. Walk carefully, the roads are long.

ambient_chatter.text: The fog over {town} is thick again this morning. I have crossed in worse weather and lived to complain about it.
Heard the millers in {village} are asking after salt again. Bring what you can spare to market, the winter will not wait.
Lag on the eastern road again. Patience is an old virtue, and the server has always been slow in the wet months.
A young rider asked me the way to {town} today and I paid his toll at the bridge. Do the same for someone next week, it is a small debt.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the field today. Every veteran has a day like that. Gather what is left and march again.
Ser {player}, losing {troop_count} men hurts. I lost more in the first war and still kept my feet. Rest, and find me after.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} men lost, and the field was not kind. I feel no joy in it, only a note for the ledger. Learn from it.
